PullRequest.Title: Agents - Open new sessions to the side with Alt-click
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334508

## Summary

Alt+click (Option+click on macOS) on **New** in the Agents window opens a new session beside the current one, keeping it visible.

Regular click and existing keyboard shortcuts are unchanged. No new buttons, dropdowns, or tooltip text.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09f304b6-1184-4b81-add9-210c3a4a19ed

## Testing

- 143 targeted tests passing, 2 pending.
- Client type-check and scoped hygiene checks passing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Regular click or keyboard shortcut opens a new session as before
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command derives the active workspace/provider target, awaits openNewSession, optionally awaits the workspace-trust prompt, synchronously creates the draft, and activates it. The new await extends command-promise completion but does not add work before the visible session update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Workspace trust request when the inherited folder requires trust
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per invocation, only for an untrusted inherited folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same New command invoked openNewSession with the same inherited folder and reached the same trust request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before draft creation; user progress depends on the trust decision

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Eager agent-backend creation and configuration resolution for a provider draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider draft startup per successful workspace-backed New invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff New action created the same provider draft and started the same backend work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started asynchronously after draft construction and not awaited by openNewSession

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check Dev Container availability for the workspace, potentially using file service and shared-process service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous probe per local provider draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same probe ran for a local draft created by the pre-diff New action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget; it does not delay opening the composer

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation; provider selection scans the small registered-provider set and grid activation scans the visible slot list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new limiter or serialization. ActionRunner awaits the command promise, but it does not serialize later clicks; this is unchanged in effective boundary concurrency because the old action also started openNewSession for every click.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing provider/session caches and current-draft replacement behavior are unchanged. Warm trusted folders skip the prompt; the changed code adds no cache key or retained entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed command and full service/provider call path were traced, including awaited and fire-and-forget boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup and trust-prompt duration vary, but their count and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; regular-click work and user-visible progress are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Alt-click opens a workspace-backed draft beside the active session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Alt-click dispatches the existing New command with toSide, follows the same trust and draft-creation path that Alt-click previously reached when the modifier was ignored, then inserts or moves the draft beside the active slot and reconciles the visible grid.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request for the inherited folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff Alt-click was handled as a regular click and reached the same trust request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup per successful click; no per-visible-session fan-out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff Alt-click created the same single draft/backend but replaced the active grid slot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the composer-opening critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fire-and-forget probe for a local draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff Alt-click triggered the same local-provider probe.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible slot count V controls two index scans, bounded array splices, and one grid reconciliation; one new SessionView is created only when side opening increases the slot count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grid mutation and UI reconciliation are synchronous and single-shot. Provider startup remains asynchronous; rapid-click overlap was already possible because Alt-click previously ran the ordinary New action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold side open creates one slot/view. If a draft already exists, replacement updates its wrapper and disposes the superseded provider draft; an existing slot/view is reused when possible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: insertion, wrapper replacement, session-part reconciliation, and provider startup paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: V can increase with user-pinned sessions and SessionView construction has nontrivial UI cost, but this is the direct requested visible-side-pane behavior rather than hidden or repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the only additional cost is the bounded rendering required to keep the requested second visible pane.

Scenarios.Scenario: Alt-click opens or reuses the folderless empty composer beside a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With no inherited folder, openNewSession performs no provider creation. It inserts or moves the single undefined slot, activates it, publishes one visible-session array, reconciles the grid, and focuses the composer.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible slot count V; the model enforces at most one empty slot, so repeated use does not grow retained state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is synchronous on the click path with no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold behavior creates one additional SessionView slot. Warm behavior moves/reuses the existing empty slot; when it is already active, activation does not republish the visible array.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the empty-slot invariant, insertion logic, observable refresh, and SessionView reuse guard were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Grid size depends on pinned sessions, but realistic cost is linear in the currently visible panes and occurs once per explicit placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; no unbounded retention, duplicate composer, or repeated external boundary is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced regular-click, workspace-backed Alt-click, and folderless Alt-click paths through action dispatch, session creation, provider boundaries, visibility ownership, grid reconciliation, and cleanup. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.
